tasks.description: Use the `csv` module to write a CSV file 'students.csv' with columns Name, Grade, Score. Include 3 student rows.
tasks.hint:
`import csv`
`with open('students.csv', 'w', newline='') as f: writer = csv.writer(f)`
`writer.writerow(['Name', 'Grade', 'Score'])` writes the header.
Then `writer.writerow(['Alice', 'A', 95])` for each student.
tasks.solution:
import csv

with open('students.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f)
    writer.writerow(['Name', 'Grade', 'Score'])
    writer.writerow(['Alice', 'A', 95])
    writer.writerow(['Bob', 'B', 87])
    writer.writerow(['Carol', 'A', 92])

print('students.csv written')
tasks.walkthrough:
The writer turns each list into one comma-separated line. The header goes first, then one row per student.
`newline=''` lets the csv module control line endings so there are no stray blank lines.

tasks.description: Read 'students.csv' back using `csv.reader`. Print each row.
tasks.hint:
`with open('students.csv', 'r') as f: reader = csv.reader(f)`
`for row in reader: print(row)` — each row is a list of strings.
The first row is the header — you may want to skip it with `next(reader)`.
tasks.solution:
import csv

with open('students.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f)
    writer.writerow(['Name', 'Grade', 'Score'])
    writer.writerow(['Alice', 'A', 95])
    writer.writerow(['Bob', 'B', 87])
    writer.writerow(['Carol', 'A', 92])

with open('students.csv', 'r', newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f)
    for row in reader:
        print(row)
tasks.walkthrough:
The file is written first so this task runs on its own.
`csv.reader` yields each line as a list of strings, header included.

tasks.description: Use `csv.DictReader` to read 'students.csv' and print each row as a dictionary (keys from the header).
tasks.hint:
`csv.DictReader(f)` automatically uses the first row as keys.
Each row is an `OrderedDict` — access by key: `row['Name']`, `row['Score']`
This is more readable than using index numbers.
tasks.solution:
import csv

with open('students.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f)
    writer.writerow(['Name', 'Grade', 'Score'])
    writer.writerow(['Alice', 'A', 95])
    writer.writerow(['Bob', 'B', 87])
    writer.writerow(['Carol', 'A', 92])

with open('students.csv', 'r', newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    for row in reader:
        print(dict(row))
tasks.walkthrough:
`DictReader` reads the header itself and uses it as the keys for every following row.
Each row is a dictionary-like object; wrapping in `dict()` prints it in the familiar form.

tasks.description: Read the scores from 'students.csv' and compute the average score. Print it formatted to 2 decimal places.
tasks.hint:
Use `DictReader` — access `row['Score']` for each row.
Convert to float: `float(row['Score'])` — CSV data is always strings.
Compute: `total / count` or `sum(scores) / len(scores)`
tasks.solution:
import csv

with open('students.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f)
    writer.writerow(['Name', 'Grade', 'Score'])
    writer.writerow(['Alice', 'A', 95])
    writer.writerow(['Bob', 'B', 87])
    writer.writerow(['Carol', 'A', 92])

with open('students.csv', 'r', newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    scores = [float(row['Score']) for row in reader]

average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print(f'Average score: {average:.2f}')
tasks.walkthrough:
The scores are read by column name and converted to floats as they're collected.
The average is the total divided by the count, formatted to two decimal places.

tasks.description: Use `csv.DictWriter` to write a list of dicts to a new CSV file. Include a proper header row.
tasks.hint:
`fieldnames = ['Name', 'Age']` — define the column order.
`writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)`
`writer.writeheader()` writes the header; `writer.writerows(list_of_dicts)` writes all data.
tasks.solution:
import csv

people = [
    {'Name': 'Alice', 'Age': 30},
    {'Name': 'Bob', 'Age': 25},
    {'Name': 'Carol', 'Age': 35},
]

with open('people.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['Name', 'Age'])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(people)

with open('people.csv', 'r') as f:
    print(f.read().strip())
tasks.walkthrough:
`fieldnames` fixes the column order. `writeheader` writes those names as the first line.
`writerows` takes the list of dictionaries and writes each one in that column order.

lesson.intro:
CSV files are the plain-text spreadsheets of the world. You wrote one by hand
on day 25. The `csv` module does the fiddly parts properly: commas inside
values, quoting, and reading rows straight into dictionaries.

sections.heading: Writing with csv.writer
sections.body:
Open the file with `newline=''` (the module handles line endings itself),
make a writer, and pass each row as a list. `writerows` takes a list of
rows at once.
sections.code:
import csv

with open('students.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f)
    writer.writerow(['Name', 'Grade', 'Score'])
    writer.writerows([['Alice', 'A', 95], ['Bob', 'B', 87]])

print(open('students.csv').read())

sections.heading: Reading with csv.reader
sections.body:
Each row comes back as a list of strings. The first row is the header;
`next(reader)` skips it if you don't want it.
sections.code:
import csv

with open('students.csv', newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f)
    header = next(reader)
    for row in reader:
        print(row)

sections.heading: DictReader: rows as dictionaries
sections.body:
`DictReader` uses the header row as keys, so you can write `row['Score']`
instead of `row[2]`. Values are still strings; convert numbers yourself.
sections.code:
import csv

with open('students.csv', newline='') as f:
    scores = [float(row['Score']) for row in csv.DictReader(f)]
print(scores)
print(f'{sum(scores) / len(scores):.2f}')

sections.heading: DictWriter: dictionaries to rows
sections.body:
Give it the column names, call `writeheader()`, then pass dictionaries.
Keys that aren't in `fieldnames` cause an error, so the columns are
always consistent.
sections.code:
import csv

people = [{'Name': 'Alice', 'Age': 30}, {'Name': 'Bob', 'Age': 25}]
with open('people.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['Name', 'Age'])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(people)

print(open('people.csv').read())

watch_out: Forgetting `newline=''` when opening for writing on Windows gives blank lines between rows.
Everything read from a CSV is a string. `'95' + '87'` is `'9587'`.
`writerow` takes one list. `writerow('abc')` writes a, b, c as three columns.
The header row is data to `csv.reader`. Skip it with `next()` if you're summing a column.
